card: Allows importing public descriptors into private-key-enabled wallets when the wallet already holds the corresponding private keys. Previously, Bitcoin Core rejected public descriptors on privkey-enabled wallets, forcing users to expose and pass sensitive private keys via RPC even if the wallet already stored the master xprv. The wallet now inspects existing ScriptPubKeyMans, substituting matching master xprvs into origin-annotated xpubs and attaching matching individual keys. Closes issue 27336.
changed_since_previous: Rebased following the merge of prerequisite PR #34861, with no functional changes to the substitution approach.
evidence: PR description: 'Currently importing a descriptor to a wallet that has private keys requires the descriptor to include the private keys. This is not ideal as it means exposing private key material.'
Linked issue #27336: 'Should be able to import an xpub descriptor to a privkey-enabled wallet if the wallet has the privkeys'
problem: Importing a descriptor into a private-key-enabled wallet fails unless the descriptor explicitly contains private keys. Users are forced to expose sensitive private key material over RPC during import even when the wallet already possesses the master xprv or required private keys.

risk.why: Flaws in key derivation or matching during descriptor substitution could bind incorrect private keys or fail to derive spending keys, risking wallet spendability or fund loss.

scope_notes: Touches both wallet import logic and descriptor AST traversal via the new SubstituteMasterExtPubs method.
summary: Allows importing public descriptors into private-key-enabled wallets when the wallet already holds the matching private keys. During descriptor import, the wallet queries its existing descriptor scriptpubkey managers for known private keys and master xprvs. It substitutes matching origin-annotated xpubs (including participants in MuSig expressions) and supplies matching individual private keys to the import signing provider.
